title: Per-head tiling and KV-windowed routing for MQA head-skew and LLaMA attention stride anomalies
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: users operating MQA models (qwen/mistral variants) observed throughput regressions on multi-head GPUs when token distributions are highly skewed by a few hot tokens. Root cause analysis showed head-wise tensor packing triggered suboptimal kernel selection and oversized KV-cache snapshots for LLaMA-style rotary/stride variants, increasing memory movement and serialization overhead. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: 1) Per-head tiling hints that allow the scheduler to choose head-local tile sizes based on observed head activation sparsity, enabling smaller kernels for skewed heads while keeping dense heads on high-throughput kernels; 2) KV-windowed routing which maintains a tunable sliding window for KV snapshot materialization per-request-group to avoid full-KV snapshots on short-context bursts and to prefer compact delta snapshots when sequence growth is small. Design notes: the changes are runtime-only and behind two feature flags (runtime.per_head_tiling, runtime.kv_windowing_delta). Per-head tiling computes head occupancy histograms over an adaptive epoch and surfaces a hint enum (COMPACT|BALANCED|THROUGHPUT) to the kernel selector. KV-windowed routing tracks per-route recent max-prefix-length and uses a small LRU-indexed ring buffer to store recent KV deltas; routing prefers delta materialization if predicted extra-memory-copy cost is less than the kernel startup amortized cost. Tests and validation: microbenchmarks across LLaMA-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen-14B-MQA with synthetic skewed prompts, real-chat replay workloads and end-to-end Redwood-hosted API workloads. Observed results: 8-18% median p99 generation latency reduction on skewed tails, 12-22% per-token throughput improvement for short-burst conversational workloads, and peak GPU memory reduction up to 9% on MQA variants. Rollout plan: feature flags default-off for 1 week of dogfooding, then opt-in on Canary, followed by controlled ramp to GA with telemetry gated thresholds. Backwards compatibility: no model format changes and kernel fallbacks for unknown hint values. See linked Linear tickets for further follow-ups and benchmarking tasks.

release_notes: Improves inference latency and throughput for skewed multi-head workloads by introducing per-head tiling and KV-windowed delta routing. Rollout is behind feature flags; enable with runtime.per_head_tiling and runtime.kv_windowing_delta. May reduce peak GPU memory for certain MQA models.
notes: This change is intentionally conservative: default flags are off. Observability was added to detect mispredictions and fallback to safe kernels automatically. Follow-up work tracked in ENG-2345 to refine the head occupancy epoch tuning.
